test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Menar, one of the newly added wetlands to Ramsar sites, is located in which state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Menar** is located in the **Udaipur district** of the state of **Rajasthan**. It has gained international recognition for its rich biodiversity and community-led conservation efforts.
 
• It is famously known as the **"Bird Village"** of **Rajasthan** because it serves as a major habitat for a wide variety of migratory and resident bird species.
 
• The wetland consists of two primary seasonal lakes, namely **Brahma Lake** and **Dhandh Lake**, which spread across approximately **400 hectares** of land.
 
• In **2022**, the **Rajasthan** state government initiated the formal process to declare Menar as a **Ramsar site**, seeking to provide it with international protection under the **Ramsar Convention**.
 
• The conservation of this wetland is unique because it is entirely managed by the local **Menaria community**, who have protected the ecosystem for centuries without formal government intervention until recently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ramsar Convention:**

 
 
• The **Ramsar Convention** on Wetlands is an intergovernmental treaty established in **1971** in the city of **Ramsar, Iran**.
 
• It provides the framework for national action and international cooperation for the conservation and wise use of **wetlands** and their resources.
 
• India became a signatory to this convention on **February 1, 1982**.
 
 
 
• **Wetlands in Rajasthan:**
 
 
• Currently, **Rajasthan** is home to two prominent **Ramsar sites**: **Keoladeo National Park** (designated in **1981**) in **Bharatpur** and **Sambhar Lake** (designated in **1990**) in **Jaipur**.
 
• Menar is slated to become the **third Ramsar site** in the state, boosting eco-tourism and conservation funding in the **Mewar region**.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity at Menar:**
 
 
• The village attracts more than **150 species** of birds every year during the winter season.
 
• Key species include the **Greater Flamingo**, **Great White Pelican**, **Bar-headed Goose**, **Northern Shoveler**, and the **Common Crane**.
 
• The presence of these birds indicates a healthy aquatic ecosystem, which the **local villagers** maintain by prohibiting fishing and harmful agricultural runoff.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Community Conservation Model:** The **Menaria community** has set a global example by voluntarily banning fishing, sand mining, and the use of chemical fertilizers near the lakes to ensure the safety of the birds.
 
• **Legal Status:** The area was notified as a **Wetland** under the **Wetland (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017**, which provides a legal shield against encroachment and pollution.
 
• **National Context:** As of **August 2024**, **India** has a total of **85 Ramsar sites**, covering an area of over **1.3 million hectares**. **Tamil Nadu** currently holds the highest number of sites (**18**), followed by **Uttar Pradesh** (**10**).
 
• **Significance of Wetlands:** Often referred to as the **"Kidneys of the Landscape,"** wetlands like Menar play a crucial role in **groundwater recharge**, carbon sequestration, and flood control.
